there's a lot to like about the game -- but a lot that's unfinished and broken. take a look at the posts on the steam discussion board about this game -- the developer promised to fix a bunch of bugs several years ago and then disappeared from the grid.

in terms of things to like -- it's a great vr mechanic the way the player is above the fray -- perfect for example if something like half-life alyx where enemies are jumping or walking strread moreaight at you is too intense. the teleportation approach is great too.

in terms of unfinished issues, buttons to rotate yourself (e.g. click to turn left, or right) do not work -- the controls to rotate don't do anything, and on some controllers like the htc vive the instructions to use the oculus buttons could never work -- posts on the boards show that even if you have the right controller, the controlls still don't work. so if you have a wire on your headset, you will find it getting in the way when you have to turn 180 or more to hit everything that's on all sides of you.

options in the settings talk about a quick swap -- your hands may get tired from holding the bow in the same hand and want to switch. there are no directions on how to do this in-game, but the setting exists, and the dev says on the boards that you can gesture to do this -- but the gesture does nothing and others have posted the same problem.

there are several other bugs like how you draw from your quiver which works sometimes and then stops working.

it's what it says it is -- fruit ninja in vr. it's fun to slice fruit in vr, but it's a very simple game.

first, the positives. if you enjoyed fruit ninja even casually, you'll enjoy this game for at least a few minutes. it's entertaining to discover you can use the side of the blade to move objects without slicing them -- you could even move a bomb out of the way, but you'd have to be very quick to use that effectively. if you're trying for the first time in read morevr, i recommend the zen or arcade mode (not classic which is unforgiving as you try it out).

the negatives: the game doesn't do much in terms of using the benefits of the vr. for one, there's only one place you ever stand, and only one perspective, with a relatively simple environment -- so if you like vr to feel like you're somewhere else, or somewhere new, this gives you less than even the basic environments that let you move to at least a few locations.

the mechanic misses out on some of the simple ideas in vr that would make this more fun and engaging -- for example, using the vibration on the controllers to help feel things.

as my first full vr puzzle experience, i was unprepared for the level of design and skill put into this game.

gameplay: 
i expect you to die begins you at your desk at hq where it teaches you how to play the game and use the controls. without spoiling too much, you'll embark on 7 exciting and brain tingling missions. 3 of these missions are dlcs that were added into the game after release. in your office, you are assigned mission after mission, but with these missions, you have a new type of clue or useful trick you've learned to help with the next missions, seamlessly throwing new techniques that make you think about each interaction. the use of your powers you inately use along the way is intuitive and amazing. a full seated experience that will leave you what feels like trapped in your headset and not wanting to leave until you stop dr. zor himself. you will mutter to yourself, curse, and even laugh as the game pokes at you and offers you a more true experience full with sassy quips and jester filled moments of laughter. the feeling of solving a puzzle is yet another reason i played this without stopping a single time. the puzzles that are designed are perfect for the spy feel. infiltrate, create, and mind trick your way through these wonderful puzzles that leave you wanting more. at the agency hq you will see collectables as you go through levels. some of these little collectibles are from completing a certain action or interaction through the level without it giving or taking from your main objective. this little addition to some is a home run for collectionists and completionists in video games. instead of collecting the items, your actions and interactions with the environment are given as clues on your mission reels so you can hunt for all the items to go in your agency office. 

conclusion:
if you are an infitiy member, or just someone looking to add a game to their collection, this one is for everyone. this game was free for me since i paid for a year of infinity, but i will now be purchasing i expect you to die 2 as soon as it releases. this studio has put out amazing and beautifully crafted games. i can say that the cost of this game is so low for the level of quality, but the devs have got to eat. now they sit on a highly rated experience of more than 4 hours that it takes to beat the game if you aren't looking up clues online and more than 4 if you plan on collecting everything the same way. all in all, this game is too good to pass up, please consider buying this and supporting the team that built this masterpiece of a game.
